predecessors.name: Jin dynasty (Western and Eastern Jin)
predecessors.text: Liaoxi Commandery, 'the Duan held Liaoxi as a ducal fief over their home commandery' (Conquest of the Duan); Wuwuchen 'was based in Liaoxi Commandery' (Duan Wuwuchen)

successors.name: Later Zhao
successors.text: Lingzhi and the cities round it: Zhao 'captured more than forty cities, and Yuyang, Shanggu, and Dai commanderies surrendered'

successors.name: Former Yan
successors.text: Liaoxi, whence 'Murong Huang returned to Yan with 5,000 households'

ledger.x: 307: Duan Wuwuchen made Duke of Liaoxi.
314: the Duan take Wang Jun's old capital.
321: Duan Pidi is captured by Later Zhao.
January 338: Later Zhao and Former Yan march on the Duan.
April 338: the campaign ends in Zhao-Yan victory.

wars.name: Shi Le's war against Wang Jun and the Duan
wars.outcome: 'In 313, after some negotiations, Jilujuan agreed with Shi Le to break off relations with Wang Jun'; 'Wang Jun was defeated by Shi Le in 314'; the Pidi branch seized Jicheng.

wars.name: Later Zhao capture of Duan Pidi
wars.outcome: 'In 321, Pidi was captured and later killed by Shi Le's state of Later Zhao'; no land is named.

wars.name: Conquest of the Duan
wars.outcome: January-April 338 campaign: Zhao took Lingzhi and more than forty cities; Yan took 5,000 households from Liaoxi; Duan Liao killed in 339 after surrendering and rebelling.

certainty.note: A tribal polity: the page gives a territory in one line ('From Yuyang Commandery to the Liao River') and nothing sharper.
